bugs.name: Bartonella henselae
bugs.symptoms: Papule at scratch site then painful regional lymphadenopathy; bacillary angiomatosis in AIDS

bugs.name: Bartonella quintana
bugs.symptoms: Relapsing fever every 5 days with severe shin and back pain; spread by body lice

bugs.name: Bartonella bacilliformis
bugs.symptoms: Acute severe hemolytic anemia then chronic blood-filled Peruvian Warts; spread by sandfly

bugs.name: Plasmodium falciparum
bugs.symptoms: Irregular fever, RBC knobs causing capillary sequestration, coma, organ failure

bugs.name: Plasmodium vivax
bugs.symptoms: 48-hour fever cycle; dormant liver hypnozoites causing relapse months later
bugs.treatment: Chloroquine plus primaquine for radical cure (check G6PD first)

bugs.name: Plasmodium ovale
bugs.symptoms: 48-hour fever cycle; dormant liver hypnozoites causing relapse
bugs.treatment: Chloroquine plus primaquine or tafenoquine for radical cure

bugs.name: Plasmodium malariae
bugs.symptoms: 72-hour quartan fever cycle; no hypnozoites

bugs.name: Babesia microti
bugs.symptoms: Hemolytic anemia and fever; Maltese cross tetrads on smear; severe in asplenics

bugs.name: Trypanosoma cruzi
bugs.symptoms: Romana's sign (swollen eye); chronic megacolon, megaesophagus, dilated cardiomyopathy

bugs.name: Trypanosoma brucei
bugs.symptoms: Winterbottom's sign (posterior cervical nodes); CNS invasion reverses sleep/wake cycle
bugs.treatment: Suramin (early) or melarsoprol (CNS); Tsetse fly vector

bugs.name: Zika virus
bugs.symptoms: Mild rash and conjunctivitis in adults; severe fetal microcephaly if infected in pregnancy

bugs.name: SARS-CoV-2
bugs.symptoms: Respiratory illness; cytokine storm causing ARDS and septic shock; binds ACE2 receptor
bugs.treatment: Dexamethasone in late inflammatory phase (harmful if given early)

bugs.name: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus)
bugs.symptoms: Acute retroviral syndrome then CD4 decline below 200 with opportunistic infections

bugs.name: HTLV-1
bugs.geography: Japan, the Caribbean, parts of Africa
bugs.symptoms: ATLL malignancy and tropical spastic paraparesis (leg weakness/rigidity)
bugs.treatment: No effective antiretroviral therapy prevents ATLL

bugs.name: Ebola virus
bugs.symptoms: Cytokine storm, vascular leak, DIC, hypovolemic shock; 50-90% mortality

bugs.name: Marburg virus
bugs.symptoms: Cytokine storm with vascular leak and hemorrhage; fruit bat reservoir

bugs.name: Yellow Fever virus
bugs.symptoms: Triad of high fever, jaundice, and black vomit; Councilman bodies on liver biopsy
bugs.treatment: Supportive care; live-attenuated vaccine for prevention

bugs.name: Dengue virus
bugs.symptoms: Breakbone fever; second infection worsened by antibody-dependent enhancement

bugs.name: Hantavirus (Sin Nombre virus)
bugs.geography: Four Corners region of US Southwest (NM, AZ, CO, UT)
bugs.symptoms: Flu-like prodrome then rapid severe pulmonary edema; deer mouse droppings exposure

bugs.name: Lassa virus
bugs.symptoms: Often mild febrile illness; sensorineural deafness in one-third of survivors

bugs.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii
bugs.symptoms: Subacute dry cough and dyspnea; ground-glass opacities; occurs at CD4 < 200

bugs.name: Toxoplasma gondii
bugs.symptoms: Headache or seizure; multiple ring-enhancing basal ganglia lesions on MRI

bugs.name: JC virus
bugs.symptoms: Subacute cognitive decline; non-enhancing white matter lesions on MRI
bugs.treatment: No specific therapy; restore immunity with ART

bugs.name: Cryptococcus neoformans
bugs.symptoms: Headache with high intracranial pressure; encapsulated yeast on India ink
bugs.treatment: Amphotericin B plus flucytosine; serial LPs for pressure

bugs.name: Mycobacterium avium complex
bugs.symptoms: High fevers, night sweats, elevated alkaline phosphatase; CD4 < 50

bugs.name: Cytomegalovirus (CMV)
bugs.symptoms: Pizza-pie retina (hemorrhage plus exudates); deep linear esophageal ulcers; CD4 < 50

bugs.name: Clostridioides difficile
bugs.symptoms: Watery diarrhea after broad-spectrum antibiotic use disrupts microbiome

drugs.name: Unfractionated Heparin
drugs.mechanism: Binds antithrombin III, accelerating inactivation of thrombin (IIa) and factor Xa

drugs.name: Low Molecular Weight Heparin (Enoxaparin)
drugs.disease: DVT/PE treatment and prophylaxis; anticoagulation in pregnancy
drugs.mechanism: Antithrombin-mediated inhibition predominantly of factor Xa
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding; lower HIT risk; accumulates in renal failure

drugs.name: Fondaparinux
drugs.disease: Anticoagulation, preferred if history of HIT
drugs.mechanism: Synthetic pentasaccharide that exclusively inhibits factor Xa via antithrombin

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits VKORC1, blocking gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding, skin necrosis, teratogenic (reverse with vitamin K or PCC/FFP)

drugs.name: Rivaroxaban / Apixaban
drugs.disease: AFib stroke prevention and DVT/PE treatment
drugs.mechanism: Direct oral inhibitors of factor Xa

drugs.name: Dabigatran
drugs.disease: AFib stroke prevention and DVT/PE treatment
drugs.mechanism: Direct oral inhibitor binding the active site of thrombin (IIa)

drugs.name: Argatroban
drugs.mechanism: Direct thrombin inhibitor

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.disease: Antiplatelet prophylaxis for MI and stroke
drugs.mechanism: Irreversibly acetylates COX-1, abolishing thromboxane A2 synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: GI ulcers; tinnitus and mixed acid-base disturbance at high doses

drugs.name: Clopidogrel
drugs.disease: Antiplatelet therapy for ACS and post-stent
drugs.mechanism: Irreversible P2Y12 ADP-receptor blocker; prodrug activated by CYP2C19
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding; ineffective in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers; rare neutropenia

drugs.name: Ticagrelor
drugs.mechanism: Reversible P2Y12 inhibitor not requiring hepatic activation
drugs.adverseEffects: Dyspnea unrelated to heart failure; bleeding

drugs.name: Abciximab
drugs.mechanism: Blocks GpIIb/IIIa receptor, preventing fibrinogen-mediated platelet aggregation

drugs.name: Alteplase (tPA)
drugs.mechanism: Converts plasminogen to plasmin, which digests the fibrin mesh of a clot
drugs.adverseEffects: Intracranial hemorrhage; contraindicated with prior ICH

drugs.name: Aminocaproic Acid / Tranexamic Acid
drugs.disease: Reversal of fibrinolytic (tPA) overdose; bleeding control
drugs.mechanism: Lysine analog that blocks plasminogen activation and binding to fibrin

drugs.name: NRTIs (Zidovudine, Tenofovir)
drugs.mechanism: Phosphorylated nucleoside analogs that cause viral DNA chain termination

drugs.name: NNRTIs (Efavirenz)
drugs.mechanism: Bind reverse transcriptase at a non-active site; no phosphorylation needed

drugs.name: Protease Inhibitors (-navir)
drugs.mechanism: Block HIV protease, preventing cleavage of polyproteins and viral maturation

drugs.name: Integrase Inhibitors (-tegravir)
drugs.mechanism: Block integrase, preventing viral DNA insertion into the host genome

drugs.name: Maraviroc
drugs.mechanism: Entry inhibitor that binds the CCR5 co-receptor blocking viral attachment
drugs.adverseEffects: Ineffective against CXCR4-tropic virus (requires tropism assay)

drugs.name: Tenofovir/Emtricitabine (PrEP)
drugs.disease: HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis in high-risk individuals
drugs.mechanism: Daily NRTI combination preventing establishment of HIV infection

drugs.name: Chloroquine / Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.mechanism: Blocks heme polymerization into hemozoin, so toxic free heme damages parasite
drugs.adverseEffects: Retinopathy and cardiotoxicity with chronic high-dose use

drugs.name: Mefloquine
drugs.mechanism: Blood schizonticide of unclear mechanism
drugs.adverseEffects: Neuropsychiatric effects including vivid dreams and frank psychosis

drugs.name: Atovaquone-Proguanil
drugs.mechanism: Atovaquone collapses parasite mitochondrial bc1; proguanil inhibits DHFR
drugs.adverseEffects: Generally well tolerated; GI upset, headache, transaminitis

drugs.name: Artemisinins (Artemether, Artesunate)
drugs.mechanism: Endoperoxide bridge cleaved by heme generates radicals damaging the parasite
drugs.adverseEffects: Generally well tolerated; black-water fever at high parasite burden

drugs.name: Quinine
drugs.mechanism: Blood schizonticide of poorly understood mechanism

drugs.name: Primaquine
drugs.disease: Radical cure of P. vivax/ovale (hypnozoite eradication)
drugs.mechanism: 8-aminoquinoline generating reactive oxygen species in parasite mitochondria
drugs.adverseEffects: Acute hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency; screen G6PD first

drugs.name: Tafenoquine
drugs.disease: Radical cure and prophylaxis of malaria
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting 8-aminoquinoline generating reactive oxygen species

drugs.name: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine
drugs.disease: Intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy (IPTp)
drugs.mechanism: Synergistic folate inhibition (blocks dihydropteroate synthase and DHFR)

drugs.name: Doxycycline (antimalarial use)
drugs.disease: Malaria prophylaxis and adjunct to quinine treatment
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits the parasite apicoplast causing delayed death
drugs.adverseEffects: Photosensitivity; tooth enamel staining (avoid age <8 and pregnancy)

drugs.name: TMP-SMX
drugs.disease: Treatment and prophylaxis of Pneumocystis pneumonia
drugs.mechanism: Sequential folate-synthesis inhibition

drugs.name: Amphotericin B
drugs.mechanism: Binds ergosterol forming membrane pores in fungal cells

drugs.name: Eculizumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody inhibiting complement C5
drugs.adverseEffects: Predisposes to Neisseria infections (impaired membrane attack complex)

correlates.name: Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP)
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies against GpIIb/IIIa drive splenic macrophage destruction of platelets
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids, IVIG; splenectomy in refractory cases

correlates.name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)
correlates.pathophysiology: ADAMTS13 deficiency leaves large vWF multimers that trap platelets into microthrombi

correlates.name: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Shiga-like toxin from E. coli O157:H7 injures endothelium causing renal microthrombi

correlates.name: Hemophilia
correlates.pathophysiology: X-linked deficiency of factor VIII (A) or factor IX (B) impairs secondary hemostasis

correlates.name: von Willebrand Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: vWF deficiency impairs platelet adhesion and destabilizes factor VIII (double hit)

correlates.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
correlates.pathophysiology: Systemic insult triggers widespread clotting that consumes platelets and factors
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying cause; transfuse platelets, FFP, cryoprecipitate

correlates.name: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: GpIb deficiency impairs platelet adhesion; giant platelets on smear

correlates.name: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia
correlates.pathophysiology: GpIIb/IIIa deficiency prevents platelet aggregation

correlates.name: Waterhouse-Friderichsen Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Bilateral adrenal hemorrhage from DIC during meningococcemia
correlates.treatment: Emergent corticosteroids and antibiotics for the sepsis

correlates.name: Factor V Leiden
correlates.pathophysiology: Mutant factor V resists inactivation by activated protein C, causing hypercoagulability

correlates.name: Pulmonary Embolism
correlates.pathophysiology: Embolized DVT lodges in the pulmonary arteries; saddle embolus causes sudden death

correlates.name: Fat Embolism Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Marrow fat enters circulation after long bone fracture

correlates.name: Trousseau Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Occult malignancy releases procoagulants causing migratory thrombophlebitis

correlates.name: Splenic Sequestration Crisis
correlates.pathophysiology: Sickle cell spleen suddenly traps a large blood volume causing hypovolemic shock

correlates.name: Aplastic Crisis
correlates.pathophysiology: Parvovirus B19 infects erythroid precursors halting RBC production (reticulocytes zero)

correlates.name: Acute Chest Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Pulmonary vaso-occlusion in sickle cell disease causing new infiltrate and hypoxia

correlates.name: Diamond-Blackfan Anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Congenital pure red cell aplasia with macrocytic anemia and triphalangeal thumbs

correlates.name: Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Rapid protein C drop on starting warfarin causes transient hypercoagulable microthrombosis
correlates.treatment: Bridge with heparin when initiating warfarin

correlates.name: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT)
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG against heparin-PF4 complexes activates platelets causing thrombosis and low counts
correlates.treatment: Stop heparin; start a direct thrombin inhibitor (argatroban)

correlates.name: Bacillary Angiomatosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Bartonella infection of vascular endothelium causes proliferative red-purple skin nodules in AIDS

correlates.name: Acute Retroviral Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Initial high-level HIV viremia 2-4 weeks after exposure causes a mononucleosis-like illness

correlates.name: AIDS
correlates.pathophysiology: Progressive HIV depletion of CD4 T-cells below 200 enabling opportunistic infections
correlates.treatment: Lifelong antiretroviral therapy plus opportunistic infection prophylaxis

correlates.name: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever
correlates.pathophysiology: Antibody-dependent enhancement on a second dengue serotype boosts viral entry and inflammation

correlates.name: Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome (IRIS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Rising CD4 count after starting ART triggers a violent inflammatory response to existing pathogen burden
correlates.treatment: Delay ART 2-4 weeks after treating the opportunistic infection

correlates.name: Cerebral (Severe) Falciparum Malaria
correlates.pathophysiology: Infected RBCs adhere to brain endothelium causing microvascular obstruction and hyperparasitemia
correlates.treatment: IV artesunate, then transition to oral ACT

correlates.name: G6PD Deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: X-linked G6PD loss prevents NADPH/glutathione regeneration, causing oxidative hemolysis
correlates.treatment: Remove oxidative trigger; supportive care; transfuse if severe

correlates.name: Black-Water Fever
correlates.pathophysiology: Massive intravascular hemolysis in severe malaria causing hemoglobinuria and AKI
